questions.question: Which Indian state has the longest coastline among all states?
questions.explanation: Gujarat has the longest coastline of any Indian state, stretching roughly 1,600 km along the Arabian Sea. Andhra Pradesh has the longest coastline on the eastern (Bay of Bengal) side, but it is shorter than Gujarat's.

questions.question: The Bhakra Nangal Dam, one of the earliest major river-valley projects of independent India, is built on which river?
questions.explanation: The Bhakra Dam is built across the Sutlej river in Himachal Pradesh, with the associated Nangal canals serving Punjab and Haryana. Beas, Ravi and Chenab are the other rivers of the Indus system in the region.

questions.question: Who is popularly known as the 'Father of the Indian Constitution'?
questions.explanation: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly and steered the preparation of the Constitution, earning him the title 'Father of the Indian Constitution'.

questions.question: Which right is guaranteed to every person by Article 21 of the Constitution of India?
options: B) Protection of life and personal liberty
C) Freedom of speech and expression
questions.explanation: Article 21 states that no person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. Equality before the law is Article 14, freedom of speech is Article 19(1)(a), and the right against exploitation is Articles 23-24.

questions.question: Kathakali, a classical dance-drama known for its elaborate facial make-up and costumes, originated in which state?
questions.explanation: Kathakali developed in Kerala and draws on stories from the Ramayana and Mahabharata. Odissi belongs to Odisha, Kuchipudi to Andhra Pradesh and Manipuri to Manipur.

questions.question: The Tropic of Cancer passes through eight Indian states. Which of the following states does it NOT pass through?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer crosses Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram. Uttarakhand lies entirely north of the Tropic in the Himalayan region.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian citizen to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences?
questions.explanation: Amartya Sen received the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences in 1998 for his work on welfare economics. Abhijit Banerjee won the 2019 Economics Nobel but as a US citizen of Indian origin; C. V. Raman (Physics, 1930) and Kailash Satyarthi (Peace, 2014) won in different categories.

questions.question: At the 2024 Paris Olympic Games, which country finished at the top of the medal table?
questions.explanation: The USA topped the Paris 2024 medal table with 126 total medals, including 40 golds — edging China, which also won 40 golds, on the countback of silvers. Host nation France finished fifth by golds.

questions.question: Which country hosted the G20 Leaders' Summit in November 2024, a year after India's New Delhi summit?
questions.explanation: The 2024 G20 Summit was held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, under Brazil's presidency. India hosted in 2023, and South Africa held the presidency and hosted the summit in 2025.

questions.question: What is the name of the lander of ISRO's Chandrayaan-3 mission, which soft-landed near the lunar south pole in August 2023?
questions.explanation: Chandrayaan-3's lander was named Vikram, after Vikram Sarabhai, the father of India's space programme. Pragyan is the rover it carried; Aditya is ISRO's solar observatory mission (Aditya-L1).

questions.question: The ICC Champions Trophy 2025 was primarily hosted by Pakistan, but the matches involving India were played in which country?
questions.explanation: Under the hybrid model agreed for the tournament, Pakistan hosted most matches while all of India's games, including the final, were played in Dubai in the United Arab Emirates.

questions.question: National Space Day of India, instituted to mark the success of Chandrayaan-3's lunar landing, is observed every year on which date?
questions.explanation: Vikram, the Chandrayaan-3 lander, touched down on the Moon on 23 August 2023, and the Government of India declared 23 August as National Space Day, first observed in 2024. 28 February is National Science Day.

questions.question: Who took oath as the 51st Chief Justice of India in November 2024, succeeding Justice D. Y. Chandrachud?
questions.explanation: Justice Sanjiv Khanna was sworn in as the 51st Chief Justice of India on 11 November 2024, the day after Justice D. Y. Chandrachud, the 50th CJI, demitted office.

questions.question: The 2024 Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to Nihon Hidankyo, an organisation representing survivors of the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki, from which country?
questions.explanation: Nihon Hidankyo is a Japanese grassroots confederation of atomic-bomb survivors (hibakusha) organisations, honoured in 2024 for its efforts towards a world free of nuclear weapons.

questions.question: Find the next term in the series: 3, 6, 11, 18, 27, ___
questions.explanation: The differences between consecutive terms are 3, 5, 7 and 9 — consecutive odd numbers. The next difference is 11, so the missing term is 27 + 11 = 38.

questions.question: Book is to Chapter as Ladder is to ___
questions.explanation: A book is made up of chapters, the way a ladder is made up of rungs — the whole-to-part relationship. Wood is the material, and climb and height describe use, not parts.

questions.question: In a certain code language, TEACHER is written as VGCEJGT. How will CHILD be written in that same code?
questions.explanation: Each letter of TEACHER is shifted two places forward in the alphabet (T→V, E→G, A→C, C→E, H→J, E→G, R→T). Applying the same shift to CHILD gives C→E, H→J, I→K, L→N, D→F, i.e., EJKNF.

questions.question: Pointing to a photograph, Ravi said, "She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son." How is the girl in the photograph related to Ravi?
questions.explanation: Ravi's grandfather's only son must be Ravi's own father. The daughter of Ravi's father is Ravi's sister.

questions.question: A man walks 5 km towards the north, turns right and walks 3 km, then turns right again and walks 5 km. How far is he now from his starting point?
questions.explanation: He walks 5 km north, then 3 km east (right of north), then 5 km south (right of east). The 5 km north and 5 km south cancel out, leaving him exactly 3 km east of the starting point.

questions.question: Complete the series: AZ, BY, CX, ___
questions.explanation: The first letters move forward: A, B, C, so the next is D. The second letters move backward: Z, Y, X, so the next is W. The answer is DW.

questions.question: If the letters of the alphabet are numbered as A = 1, B = 2, ..., Z = 26, and the word CAT is coded as 3-1-20, what will be the code for DOG?
questions.explanation: Using the position numbers: D is the 4th letter, O is the 15th and G is the 7th. So DOG is coded as 4-15-7.

questions.question: A is the sister of B. C is the mother of B. D is the father of C. E is the mother of D. How is A related to D?
questions.explanation: C is the mother of B and therefore also of A, so C is A's mother. D is the father of C, making D A's maternal grandfather. Since A is female, A is D's granddaughter. E is one generation above D and thus A's great-grandmother.

questions.question: In an examination, a student scored 336 marks out of a maximum of 480 marks. What percentage of the maximum marks did the student score?
Two numbers are in the ratio 5 : 7. If their difference is 12, what is the sum of the two numbers?
questions.explanation: Let the numbers be 5x and 7x. Their difference 7x − 5x = 2x = 12, so x = 6. The sum is 5x + 7x = 12x = 72.

questions.question: The average of five numbers is 24. If one number, 28, is removed from the set, what is the average of the remaining four numbers?
questions.explanation: Total of the five numbers = 5 × 24 = 120. Removing 28 leaves 120 − 28 = 92. The new average = 92 / 4 = 23.

questions.question: A shopkeeper buys a pressure cooker for ₹800 and sells it for ₹920. What is his profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Profit = 920 − 800 = ₹120. Profit percentage = (120 / 800) × 100 = 15%.

questions.question: Find the compound interest on ₹5,000 at 10% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually.
questions.explanation: Amount after 2 years = 5000 × (1.10)² = 5000 × 1.21 = ₹6,050. Compound interest = 6050 − 5000 = ₹1,050. (Simple interest would have been only ₹1,000.)

questions.question: A can complete a piece of work in 12 days and B can complete the same work in 18 days. Working together, how long will they take to finish the work?
questions.explanation: A's one-day work = 1/12 and B's = 1/18. Together: 1/12 + 1/18 = 3/36 + 2/36 = 5/36 per day. Time taken = 36/5 = 7.2 days.

questions.question: A train 150 metres long crosses a stationary pole in 9 seconds. What is the speed of the train in kilometres per hour?
questions.explanation: Speed = distance / time = 150 / 9 = 50/3 m/s. Converting to km/h: (50/3) × (18/5) = 60 km/h.

questions.question: How many trailing zeros does the number 100! (100 factorial) end with?
questions.explanation: Trailing zeros come from factors of 10 = 2 × 5, and factors of 5 are the limiting ones. Count factors of 5 in 100!: floor(100/5) = 20 and floor(100/25) = 4 extra from multiples of 25. Total = 20 + 4 = 24 trailing zeros.

questions.question: If 3x − 7 = 20, what is the value of x?
questions.explanation: Adding 7 to both sides: 3x = 27. Dividing by 3: x = 9.

questions.question: What is the area of a circle of radius 7 cm? (Take π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: Area = πr² = (22/7) × 7 × 7 = 22 × 7 = 154 cm². (44 cm² is the circumference, a common confusion.)

questions.question: What is the simple interest on ₹1,200 at 5% per annum for 3 years?

A bookstore recorded its sales over four consecutive days as follows — Monday: 120 books; Tuesday: 150 books; Wednesday: 90 books; Thursday: 140 books. What was the average number of books sold per day over these four days?
questions.explanation: Total books sold = 120 + 150 + 90 + 140 = 500. Average = 500 / 4 = 125 books per day.

questions.question: The marked price of a jacket is ₹500. A shop offers a discount of 20% followed by a further discount of 10% on the reduced price. What is the final selling price of the jacket?
questions.explanation: After the 20% discount: 500 × 0.80 = ₹400. After the further 10% discount: 400 × 0.90 = ₹360. The two successive discounts are equivalent to a single 28% discount, not 30%.

questions.question: The population of a town increases by 10% in the first year and then decreases by 10% in the following year. What is the net change in the population over the two years?
questions.explanation: Take the initial population as 100. After a 10% rise it becomes 110. A 10% fall on 110 removes 11, leaving 99. So the population is 1 less than the starting 100 — a net decrease of 1%.

questions.question: In an examination, a candidate scoring 25% of the maximum marks fails by 30 marks, while another candidate scoring 45% gets 10 marks more than the pass mark. What are the maximum marks for the examination?
questions.explanation: Let the maximum marks be M and the pass mark be P. Then 0.25M = P − 30 and 0.45M = P + 10. Subtracting the first from the second: 0.20M = 40, so M = 200. (The pass mark is 0.25 × 200 + 30 = 80.)

questions.question: Statements: All squares are rectangles. All rectangles are quadrilaterals. Consider the conclusions: I. All squares are quadrilaterals. II. Some quadrilaterals are squares. Which conclusions follow?
options: B) Both Conclusion I and II follow
D) Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: Since all squares lie inside rectangles and all rectangles lie inside quadrilaterals, every square is a quadrilateral — Conclusion I follows. Because at least one square exists, those squares are quadrilaterals, so some quadrilaterals are squares — Conclusion II also follows.

questions.question: Five friends P, Q, R, S and T are sitting in a row facing north. Q sits between P and R. S sits immediately to the right of R. T sits at the extreme left end of the row. Who sits at the extreme right end?
questions.explanation: T is at the extreme left. Since Q sits between P and R and S must be immediately right of R, the row from left to right is T, P, Q, R, S. Hence S is at the extreme right end.

questions.question: If today is Monday, what day of the week will it be after 61 days?
questions.explanation: Days repeat in a cycle of 7. 61 divided by 7 gives 8 complete weeks with remainder 5. Counting 5 days from Monday: Tuesday (1), Wednesday (2), Thursday (3), Friday (4), Saturday (5). So it will be Saturday.

questions.question: What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 3:30?
questions.explanation: At 3:30, the minute hand is at the 6 and the hour hand is midway between 3 and 4. The gap between them is 2.5 hour-marks, and each hour-mark equals 30°. So the angle is 2.5 × 30 = 75°. (Equivalently, |30×3 − 5.5×30| = |90 − 165| = 75°.)

questions.question: Five children were born at intervals of exactly 3 years each. The sum of the ages of all five children today is 50 years. What is the age of the youngest child?
questions.explanation: Let the youngest be x years old. The ages are x, x+3, x+6, x+9 and x+12. Their sum is 5x + 30 = 50, so 5x = 20 and x = 4 years.

questions.question: Six friends A, B, C, D, E and F are sitting around a circular table, all facing the centre. A sits directly opposite D. B sits to the immediate right of A, and C sits to the immediate right of B. F sits directly opposite C. Who sits directly opposite E?
questions.explanation: Number the six seats 1 to 6 around the table and place A at seat 1. Moving in the direction of A's immediate right, the next two seats are B (seat 2) and C (seat 3). D, directly opposite A, occupies seat 4. F, directly opposite C, occupies seat 6. The only remaining seat, 5, goes to E, and the seat directly opposite seat 5 is seat 2 — B.

questions.question: In a row of 40 students, Rahul is 12th from the left end. What is his position from the right end?
questions.explanation: Position from the right = (Total students) − (Position from the left) + 1 = 40 − 12 + 1 = 29. So Rahul is 29th from the right end.

questions.question: If 1 January 2025 fell on a Wednesday, on what day of the week did 1 March 2025 fall? (2025 is not a leap year.)
questions.explanation: January has 31 days and February 2025 has 28 days, so 1 March is 59 days after 1 January. 59 ÷ 7 = 8 weeks with remainder 3. Wednesday plus 3 days gives Saturday.

questions.question: Deficiency of which vitamin is the most common cause of night blindness?
questions.explanation: Vitamin A is essential for the production of rhodopsin, the pigment that rod cells in the retina need for low-light vision. Its deficiency causes night blindness; severe prolonged deficiency can lead to complete blindness.

questions.question: Which gas accounts for the largest share of human-caused greenhouse gas emissions by volume and is the biggest driver of human-made climate change?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide, released mainly by burning fossil fuels and deforestation, makes up roughly three-quarters of global human-caused greenhouse emissions. Methane traps more heat per molecule but is emitted in far smaller quantities.

questions.question: Which instrument is used to measure atmospheric pressure?
questions.explanation: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure. A hygrometer measures humidity, an anemometer measures wind speed, and a manometer measures the pressure of gases in closed containers.

questions.question: Acid rain, which damages forests, lakes and buildings, is primarily caused by which two pollutants released into the atmosphere?
options: A) Sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides
questions.explanation: Sulphur dioxide (mainly from burning coal and oil) and nitrogen oxides (mainly from vehicle exhausts) react with water vapour in the atmosphere to form sulphuric acid and nitric acid, which fall as acid rain.

questions.question: Malaria is transmitted to humans by the bite of which vector?
questions.explanation: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites transmitted through the bite of the female Anopheles mosquito. The Aedes mosquito spreads dengue and chikungunya, while the Culex mosquito spreads filariasis and Japanese encephalitis.
